name: Deliver capital projects from release to in-service and closeout
summary: Capital project managers take a project released in the annual capital plan (a cable or pole line renewal, a feeder extension, a switchgear or station upgrade, a road-work relocation) and carry it through scope, design, City consent, materials, contracted civil work, in-house electrical construction, inspection, energization and financial closeout. They depend on the design group, the City's right-of-way office, a civil contractor, work planning for crew time, the control room for outages and the construction inspectors for the inspections the Electrical Distribution Safety regulation requires before energizing. Projects are slow because each handoff has a queue, City consent and contractor mobilization take weeks, and capital work competes with customer connections and trouble work for the same crews; in 2021 labour, material and pandemic outage limits deferred part of the plan.

baseline.org_archetype: A city-owned Ontario local distribution company serving about 346,000 customers with about 570 staff and an 80-person asset management and engineering division, modelled mainly on Hydro Ottawa.
baseline.notes: Reference period 2019 to 2022. 2020 non-critical projects were briefly suspended for COVID-19; in 2021 92% of planned System Renewal and System Service spending was completed.

trigger: A project in the board-approved capital program is released to project delivery, or a developer agreement or City relocation request creates a capital job.
end_state: The new plant is energized, as-builts are in GIS, the contractor is paid and holdback released, and the work order is closed and put in service for capitalization; or the project is deferred to the next year or cancelled.

volume.seasonality: Most projects are released in January to March after budget approval; civil and overhead construction runs April to November because frost, snow and winter peak loads limit excavation and outages; closeouts bunch in November and December.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate kept: about 200 projects a year inside about 35 budget programs (ho_cir2022) and a $100M program; programmatic work such as pole replacement is packaged into projects of a few streets each.

surge.cause: major storm leaving rebuild and replacement projects (for example the May 2022 derecho)

evidence.note: The derecho damaged more than 500 poles and added $15.3M of capital, four years of emergency replacements in two weeks; the follow-on permanent rebuild share and duration are the author's estimate.

Seven capital project managers; about six FTE on project delivery, the rest on capital planning estimates and relocation negotiations. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Projects manager releases funding, signs design approvals and handles escalations. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Capital design share of the design group's time (survey, drawings, material lists); customer connection design is in other processes. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Six inspectors; about two FTE on capital project civil and pre-energization inspections. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.
Schedules crew time for capital work orders. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.
Books planned outages and writes switching orders for tie-ins. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.
Executes energization switching from the control room. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

systems.name: ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
Document management and engineering drawing repository
Mobile workforce management and field tablets
SCADA for stations and feeder devices
Time entry for crews and staff
Ontario One Call member portal and locate management
City of Ottawa right-of-way Municipal Consent and road cut permit applications

resources.name: Light vehicle (pickup or van) for locators, meter technicians, inspectors and field service

steps.name: Open the project from the released program
steps.description: The project manager picks up the next project assigned from the released capital program, opens the ERP project and work order under the right budget program and investment category, and pulls the planning or condition study that justified it.

evidence.note: Capital spending is tracked by budget program and investment category; backlog wait estimated.

steps.name: Define scope, estimate and schedule
steps.description: The project manager writes a one-page charter: scope by street or station, constraints (City works, outage windows, frost), a class 3 estimate from unit costs, and a schedule that fits the construction season and crew plan.

error.defect_description: Estimate misses road restoration or a duct bank section; schedule ignores an outage window.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Engineering manager releases funding
steps.description: The projects manager reviews the charter against the approved budget line and releases the work order for design and spending, sends it back for a sharper estimate, or defers it if the program is over-committed.

control.basis: Corporate delegation of authority: release of capital work order spending

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Drive to the site for survey
steps.description: A design technologist assigned from the design queue takes a pool vehicle to the project streets or station to see the plant, clearances, trees, driveways and other utilities.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Survey the site
steps.description: On site the technologist walks the route, measures spans and setbacks, photographs poles, vaults and padmounts, notes conflicts with other utilities and trees, and checks the GIS record against what is there.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Prepare the design package
steps.description: Back at the desk the technologist draws the design to the utility's construction standards in CAD and GIS, builds the material list and construction units, and prepares the drawing set needed for City consent.

error.defect_description: Conflict with another utility missed; wrong material code or quantity.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Engineer reviews and approves the design
steps.description: A professional engineer checks the design against standards, loading and clearances and approves it under the utility's Ontario Regulation 22/04 compliance program, or returns it with markups.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 22/04 s. 7: installation work based on plans prepared and approved by a professional engineer or to approved standard designs

evidence.note: Section 7 plan approval requirement; return rate estimated.

steps.name: Apply for Municipal Consent
steps.description: The project manager submits the drawing set and cover letter to the City's right-of-way office for Municipal Consent, which circulates it to other utilities and City departments for comments and conditions.

control.basis: City of Ottawa Road Activity By-law: Municipal Consent before excavating in the right-of-way

evidence.note: Municipal Consent and circulation required before right-of-way excavation.

steps.name: Raise material requisitions
steps.description: While consent is in circulation, the project manager raises requisitions in the ERP for cable, transformers, switchgear and poles not stocked, with required-on-site dates, and reserves stocked items.

error.defect_description: Long-lead item ordered late or with the wrong rating.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: City circulates and issues consent
steps.description: The City and other right-of-way occupants review the drawings and return comments; conflicts with water, sewer, gas or telecom plant or with planned City works can require a redesign. When objections are cleared the City issues consent with conditions.

evidence.note: Circulation to other occupants for comments and conditions; durations estimated.

steps.name: Release civil work to the contractor
steps.description: The project manager issues a work release to the civil contractor on the standing unit-price contract with the drawings, consent conditions and dates, and confirms the road cut permit and traffic plan the contractor must obtain.

evidence.note: Civil work mostly contracted on standing agreements (organisation file); release timing estimated.

steps.name: Contractor mobilizes, obtains locates and road cut permit
steps.description: The contractor fits the job into its crew schedule, requests locates through Ontario One Call, obtains the road cut permit and traffic control plan, and mobilizes once locates are valid.

control.basis: Ontario Underground Infrastructure Notification System Act, 2012: locates before excavation

evidence.note: One Call locate timelines and contractor scheduling from general knowledge; source not opened.

steps.name: Contractor builds civil infrastructure
steps.description: The contractor's crew trenches or bores, lays ducts, sets vaults, padmount bases and handholes, backfills and restores the road and boulevard. Work stops for heavy rain, frost or a conflict found in the ground.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 213/91 (Construction Projects): trenching, traffic protection and excavation safety

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Drive to the civil site for inspection
steps.description: A construction inspector drives a pool vehicle to the site while the civil work is open, usually combining visits to several capital and connection jobs in one day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Inspect civil works
steps.description: The inspector checks duct depth and spacing, vault and base placement, bedding and backfill against the drawings and standards, and records deficiencies with photos on the tablet.

control.basis: Pre-job hazard assessment and Ontario Regulation 213/91 trench entry rules

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Contractor corrects deficiencies
steps.description: The contractor schedules a crew to return and fix shallow ducts, misaligned bases or poor road and boulevard restoration, then asks the inspector to re-inspect the corrected work.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Issue the capital work order to work planning
steps.description: The project manager confirms materials are on hand and sends the electrical construction work order to work planning with the design, crew-hour estimate and required outage windows.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Work planner schedules crews
steps.description: The work planner fits the job into the line or cable crew schedule against connections, maintenance and trouble work, and gives it a construction week. Jobs wait when crews, bucket trucks or materials are short or emergency work takes priority.

next.condition: deferred to next year for labour, material or outage limits

evidence.note: 2021 deferrals for labour availability, material availability and pandemic outage restrictions; DSP implementation 92%. Deferral share set to match.

steps.name: Book the planned outage and switching
steps.description: The switching planner books the outage window with the control room, writes the switching order for the tie-ins and triggers the planned outage notice to affected customers.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code and switching procedures: written switching order for planned outages

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Track electrical construction and resolve field issues
steps.description: In-house line or cable crews build the electrical work over one or more construction weeks while the project manager visits, answers crew questions, approves field changes and records progress and cost against the estimate.

next.condition: field change needs a revised design
crew pulled to emergency work, rescheduled

evidence.note: Electrical work done by in-house crews (organisation file); crews diverted to storms and connections. Durations estimated.

steps.name: Drive to the site for pre-energization inspection
steps.description: A construction inspector drives a pool vehicle to the completed job for the inspection the safety regulation requires before the new plant can be energized and connected to customers.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Verify construction before energization
steps.description: The inspector checks the installation against the approved design and standards (clearances, grounding, connections, labelling), records the result in the construction verification record, and either approves energization or lists deficiencies for the crew.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 22/04 s. 8: construction inspected and approved before the system is put into service

evidence.note: Section 8 requires inspection by a professional engineer, a qualified person under an approved construction verification program or ESA before energization.

steps.name: Energize under the switching order
steps.description: The system operator executes the switching order with the crew in the field, energizes the new plant, returns the feeder to its normal configuration and records the change in SCADA and OMS.

control.basis: Utility Work Protection Code: control room authority over switching and work protection

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Collect as-builts and send to GIS
steps.description: The project manager chases the crew's redlined drawings and the contractor's civil as-builts, checks them against the design and sends the package to the GIS team to update the network model.

error.defect_description: As-built differs from what was built (cable route, switch numbers), leaving GIS wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Approve final contractor invoice and release holdback
steps.description: The project manager checks the contractor's final quantities against inspection records, approves the invoice in the ERP, and releases the 10% holdback once the lien period has passed without claims.

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act: 10% holdback retained until the lien period expires

evidence.note: Construction Act holdback and lien periods from general knowledge; source not opened.

steps.name: Close the work order and put it in service
steps.description: The project manager reviews final cost against the estimate, writes the variance explanation, confirms all charges are in, and requests in-service and closure so accounting can capitalize the assets by asset class.

error.defect_description: Late charges or wrong asset class left on the work order.

evidence.note: Capital additions tracked against approved amounts; closeout timing estimated.

exceptions.name: Deferred for crews, materials or outage limits
exceptions.description: Crews, materials or outage windows are not available in the year and the job is carried into next year's plan.

exceptions.name: City consent conflict
exceptions.description: Circulation finds a conflict with other plant or planned City works, and the design is revised and resubmitted.

exceptions.name: Civil deficiencies
exceptions.description: The inspector finds shallow ducts, misplaced bases or poor restoration; the contractor returns.

exceptions.name: Field change during construction
exceptions.description: Crews find conditions that differ from the design and the design is revised mid-construction.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from project release to work order closeout
benchmarks.population: Distribution capital projects at a large Ontario LDC, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: most renewal and capacity projects released in Q1 are built in one construction season and closed after holdback, 7 to 10 months; projects with consent conflicts or deferrals run past a year.

benchmarks.unit: share of planned System Renewal and System Service spending completed
calendar days from leave-to-construct application (May 2019) to planned energization (Q2 2022)

evidence.note: Energization quarter taken as mid-Q2 2022; not representative of ordinary projects.

pain_points.description: Capital jobs wait for crew time because connections, maintenance and storm work draw on the same line and cable crews; some are deferred to the next year.

evidence.note: 2021 deferrals for labour, materials and outage restrictions.

pain_points.description: City consent circulation and contractor mobilization add weeks, and a conflict found in circulation sends the design back.

evidence.note: Circulation to other right-of-way occupants for comments and conditions; durations estimated.

pain_points.description: Design queues are long because the same technologists design customer connections with service-standard deadlines.

evidence.note: Organisation file sizes the design group to about 5,000 connections a year plus capital design.

pain_points.description: As-builts arrive late or differ from what was built, delaying closeout and leaving GIS out of date.

evidence.note: Common LDC records problem; estimate.

pain_points.description: Material and supply chain delays in 2021-2022 held up fleet and equipment and pushed jobs out.

evidence.note: COVID-related supply chain issues and material availability cited.

assumptions: Electrical construction labour by line and cable crews is counted in the ops construction processes (ops-overhead-construction, ops-underground-construction, ops-pole-replacement); here the construction period appears as wait time on the project manager's tracking step, so crew vehicles are not attached as resources to avoid double counting.
Construction inspection steps overlap with the separate ae-construction-inspection process; only the two inspections per project are modelled here.

Triggers keep the organisation file's capital plan, developer and relocation sources; as-builts, design packages and inspection findings are treated as inputs returned to the project, not as triggers.

Construction inspectors, work planners, switching planners and system operators take part though the organisation file's process map lists only project managers, the engineering manager and design technologists.

Contractor civil construction is entered as external waits (elapsed weeks on site, including weather stops) with no touch time, because contractor labour is outside the organisation; the contractor's cost is in the project's material and contract spend, not in labour cost per case.
The 8% deferral share is set so that about 92% of planned work completes in the year, matching 2021 DSP implementation; most projects are not deferred.

The simulated p90 (about 340 days) is below the 480-day benchmark p90 because a deferred project ends this case at the scheduling step and returns as a new case in next year's plan; the benchmark counts the carried-over project end to end.
Ontario One Call and Construction Act rules are named from general knowledge; their source pages were not opened.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa 2021-2025 Custom IR Application, UPDATED Exhibit 1-1-8 Executive Summary (EB-2019-0261), May 5, 2020
sources.supports: DSP is the culmination of business strategy, customer engagement, capital investment, asset management and regional planning processes; 2021-2025 capital by OEB category averaging $100.8M net a year; forecast went through iterations for priority, customer preference, rate impacts, resource capacity and financing; 19% of assets past expected service life (51% of stations, 23% of overhead assets), 17% in poor or very poor condition; custom scorecard measures for stations and feeders exceeding planning capacity; nearly 21,000 customers took part in rate engagement.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa 2021-2025 Custom IR Application, UPDATED Exhibit 2 (rate base), including Exhibit 2-4-1 Capital Expenditure Summary (EB-2019-0261), May 5, 2020
sources.publisher: Hydro Ottawa Limited (OEB Regulatory Document Search)
sources.supports: Rationalization process: an engineering asset needs forecast first, then a review of asset needs, safety, reliability, growth, resource constraints, rate impacts, customer input and financing that cut the forecast by about $50M a year; top four drivers (customer service requests, failure risk, system capital investment support, capacity constraints); Cambrian MTS needed because South Nepean reached the limits of local transformation capacity, leave to construct applied for May 2019, approved October 2019, energization Q2 2022; System Renewal and System Service merged for tracking because funds shift between them; commitment to ISO 55000.

sources.title: Scorecard - Hydro Ottawa Limited (2017-2021) and 2021 Scorecard Management Discussion and Analysis
sources.supports: DSP implementation progress measured as actual over planned System Renewal and System Service spending; 92% in 2021, missed because planned work was deferred for labour availability, material availability and pandemic outage restrictions; emergency spend $8.57M against a $6.73M budget, driven by poles and underground transformers.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa 2022 OEB Custom Incentive Rate Progress Report
sources.publisher: Hydro Ottawa Limited (OEB Regulatory Document Search)
sources.supports: Capital spending tracked against approved amounts by budget program (about 35 programs across System Access, System Renewal and Service, General Plant); 2021-2022 cumulative gross capital $276.4M actual vs $282.3M approved; System Service 26% under approved (capacity upgrades, SCADA, communications deferred) while System Renewal ran over; May 2022 derecho damaged more than 500 poles, cost $24M including $15.3M capital, the equivalent of four years of emergency replacements in two weeks; fleet replacement delayed by supply chain; wood pole replacement unit cost $8,415 (2021) and $9,951 (2022) against an $8,510 target.

sources.title: Ontario Regulation 22/04, Electrical Distribution Safety (Electricity Act, 1998)
sources.supports: Section 7: before installation work starts, a distributor ensures it is based on plans prepared by a professional engineer and reviewed and approved; section 8: before a new or modified distribution system is put into service its construction is inspected and approved by a professional engineer, by qualified persons in an ESA-approved construction verification program, or by the Authority; the engineer prepares a record and certificate.

sources.title: Utilities approvals (Municipal Consent and Utility Circulation)
sources.supports: Utilities need Municipal Consent to occupy and excavate a location in the public right-of-way; drawing packages are circulated to other right-of-way occupants and stakeholders for comments and conditions; work must comply with the Road Activity By-law; road cut permits are a separate process.

sources.title: An inside look at how Hydro Ottawa replaces electricity infrastructure
sources.supports: Condition is scored from visual inspections, electrical testing and infrared scans plus loading and location data into a health index; poor and very poor assets are prioritized by risk to reliability, safety and the environment; pole replacements on busy corners need City coordination to limit road closures and planned outages; underground cable work needs clear communication with customers whose property is crossed.
